topics.title: Food

questions.text: Do you have favorite food?
questions.answer: Yes, I do. I’d say my favorite food is noodles, especially the kind you can find in local restaurants. What I like most about noodles is that they’re very versatile. You can have them in soup, stir-fried, or with different toppings, so I never really get bored of them. Also, they remind me of home, so there’s a bit of an emotional connection as well.

questions.text: Is there any food you don't like?
questions.answer: Yes, there is. I’m not a big fan of very spicy food. It’s not that I can’t eat it at all, but if a dish is too spicy, it kind of ruins the whole experience for me. I can’t really taste the flavor of the food, and I end up focusing on how uncomfortable it feels instead of enjoying the meal.

questions.text: What kind kind of food did you like when you were a child?
questions.answer: When I was a child, I loved eating fried chicken and sweet rice with condensed milk. These foods were comforting and full of flavor, which made them my favorites during family meals.

questions.text: Do you eat different food at different times of the year?
questions.answer: Yes, I do change my food choices with the seasons. In winter, I prefer warm, hearty meals like soups and stews, while in summer, I enjoy fresh fruits, salads, and lighter dishes to stay cool. Seasonal eating also means using locally available ingredients, which taste better and are more nutritious.

topics.title: Day off

questions.text: When was the last time you had a few days off?
questions.answer: The last time I had a few days off was a couple of months ago, during a short holiday. I didn’t travel very far. Most of the time, I just stayed at home and tried to slow down a bit. I caught up on sleep, watched some shows, and basically gave myself a break from my usual routine.

questions.text: What do you usually do when you have days off?
questions.answer: On my days off, I usually relax at home, catch up on sleep, and go for a walk in the park to clear my mind. I also spend time reading or watching movies to unwind.

questions.text: Do you usually spend your days off with your parents or with your friends?
questions.answer: It really depends on the situation. If it’s a longer break, I tend to spend more time with my parents, because we don’t get to see each other that often. But if it’s just a single day off, I usually meet up with friends, maybe grab a meal together or just hang out and chat.

questions.text: What would you like to do if you had a day off tomorrow?
questions.answer: If I had a day off tomorrow, I’d probably keep things simple. I’d like to sleep in, go out for a nice meal, and maybe take a walk to clear my head. I wouldn’t plan anything too packed. For me, a good day off is more about relaxing and recharging than doing something special.

topics.title: Pets and Animals

questions.text: Do you like animals?
questions.answer: Yes, I do. I wouldn’t say I’m a huge animal lover, but I generally enjoy being around animals. They make people feel more relaxed, and sometimes just watching them can be quite comforting, especially after a long day.

questions.text: What's your favourite animal?
questions.answer: My favourite animal is probably dogs. What I like most about dogs is that they’re very loyal and easy to connect with. They seem to understand human emotions quite well, and being with a dog usually puts me in a better mood.

questions.text: Did you want to keep a pet when you were young?
questions.answer: Yes, I did. When I was young, I really wanted to have a pet, especially a dog. However, my parents were quite busy, and they didn’t think we had enough time or energy to take proper care of an animal, so it never really happened.

questions.text: Where do you prefer to keep your pet？indoors or outdoors？
questions.answer: I personally prefer to keep pets indoors. For one thing, it’s easier to take care of them and keep an eye on their health. Also, pets are more like family members nowadays, so I feel they should share the living space with us instead of being left outside.

questions.text: What's the most popular animal in China？
questions.answer: I’d say dogs are probably the most popular animals in China nowadays. More and more people are keeping dogs as pets, especially in cities. They’re seen not only as companions but also as part of the family, which explains why pet-related services have become so common.

topics.title: Sports team

questions.text: Have you ever been part of a sports team?
questions.answer: Yes, I have, but only at school. When I was a student, I was part of a basketball team for a short time. I wouldn’t say I was very good at it, but I really enjoyed the team atmosphere. Training and playing together helped me learn how to cooperate with others.

questions.text: Do you have a team to support?
questions.answer: Yes, I do. I support a sports team, but I wouldn’t call myself a hardcore fan. I usually follow their major games and check the results from time to time. Supporting a team makes watching sports more interesting and gives me something to talk about with friends.

questions.text: Do you like watching team games？why？
questions.answer: Yes, I really enjoy watching team games—especially football and basketball—because they’re incredibly exciting and full of unpredictable moments. What makes them special is the strong sense of teamwork and strategy; it’s fascinating to see how players communicate, adapt, and support each other under pressure. Plus, cheering for a team creates a feeling of community—I often watch matches with friends or family, and sharing that energy makes the experience even more enjoyable.

questions.text: What are the differences between team sports and individual sports？
questions.answer: Team sports, like football or basketball, require cooperation and communication among players to achieve a common goal, fostering teamwork and social skills. Individual sports, such as tennis or swimming, focus more on personal responsibility and self-motivation, allowing athletes to rely solely on their own performance. Therefore, team sports build collaboration, while individual sports develop independence.

topics.title: Reading

questions.text: Have you read any books lately?
questions.answer: Yes, I have. Recently, I’ve been reading a few non-fiction books in my spare time. I don’t read for very long each day, but I try to read a little before going to bed, which helps me relax.

questions.text: Do you prefer speed reading or thoughtful reading?
questions.answer: I personally prefer thoughtful reading. I like to take my time and really understand what the writer is trying to say. For me, reading is more about quality than speed.

questions.text: Why do some people like speed reading?
questions.answer: I think some people like speed reading because it saves time. They may have a lot of information to go through, especially for work or study, so speed reading helps them get the main ideas quickly.

questions.text: Do you like reading?
questions.answer: Definitely, I love reading! I’m a big fan of fiction, especially mystery novels, as they help me unwind after a long day. I also read self-help books occasionally to learn new skills and stay motivated. I usually read for half an hour before bed, and I find it really helps me relax and clear my mind. Reading is not just a hobby for me—it’s a way to expand my knowledge and keep my mind active.

topics.title: Keys

questions.text: Do you always bring a lot of keys with you?
questions.answer: No, not really. I try to keep my keychain simple. I usually only carry the keys that I actually need, like my house key, so it’s easier to manage.

questions.text: Have you ever lost your keys?
questions.answer: Yes, I have, and it was quite stressful. I spent a long time looking for them and felt really annoyed. Since then, I’ve been more careful about where I put my keys.

questions.text: Do you often forget the keys and lock yourself out?
questions.answer: Not very often, but it has happened once or twice. After that, I developed a habit of checking my keys before leaving home, which has helped a lot.

questions.text: Do you think it's a good idea to leave your keys with a neighbour?
questions.answer: Yes, I think it can be a good idea, as long as you trust your neighbour. It can be very helpful in emergencies, especially if you accidentally lock yourself out.

topics.title: Morning time

questions.text: Do you like getting up early in the morning?
questions.answer: It depends. On weekdays, I don’t really enjoy getting up early because I feel quite tired. But if I don’t have much pressure, I actually like early mornings because they’re quiet and peaceful.

questions.text: What do you usually do in the morning?
questions.answer: In the morning, I usually get ready for the day, have a simple breakfast, and check my phone for messages or news. After that, I head out to work or start my daily tasks.

questions.text: What did you do in the morning when you were little? Why?
questions.answer: When I was little, my mornings were quite simple. I usually got up, had breakfast, and then went to school. Everything was arranged by my parents, so I didn’t have to think too much.

questions.text: Are there any differences between what you do in the morning now and what you did in the past?
questions.answer: Yes, definitely. Now my mornings are more rushed and stressful, while in the past they were much more relaxed. I also have more responsibilities now, so I need to plan my time better.

questions.text: Do you spend your mornings doing the same things on weekends and weekdays? Why?
questions.answer: No, not really. On weekdays, my mornings are quite fixed because of work. On weekends, I prefer to slow down, sleep a bit longer, and do things more casually, since I don’t have a tight schedule.

topics.title: Gifts

questions.text: Have you ever sent handmade gifts to others?
questions.answer: Yes, I have, but not very often. I’ve made some simple handmade gifts, like cards or small crafts, mainly for close friends. I think handmade gifts feel more personal, even if they’re not very professional.

questions.text: Have you ever received a great gift?
questions.answer: Yes, I have. One of the best gifts I’ve received was something I really needed at the time. It wasn’t very expensive, but it showed that the person understood me well, which made it special.

questions.text: What do you consider when choosing a gift?
questions.answer: When choosing a gift, I mainly think about the person’s interests and needs. I also consider the occasion and my budget. For me, a suitable gift is more important than an expensive one.

questions.text: Do you think you are good at choosing gifts?
questions.answer: I’d say I’m okay at it, but not especially good. I usually spend some time thinking and comparing options, but I still feel a bit unsure sometimes. I guess I’m getting better with experience.

questions.text: What gift have you received recently?
questions.answer: Recently, I received a small but thoughtful gift from a friend. It was something practical that I can use in my daily life. Even though it was simple, it made me feel appreciated.

topics.title: Walking

questions.text: Do you walk a lot?
questions.answer: Yes, I do walk quite a lot in my daily life. I usually walk when I go to nearby places, and sometimes I take a walk just to relax and clear my mind.

questions.text: Did you often go outside to have a walk when you were a child?
questions.answer: Yes, I did. When I was a child, I often went outside to walk or play with friends, especially after dinner. It was a simple way to relax, and there weren’t many electronic devices back then.

questions.text: Why do people like to walk in parks?
questions.answer: I think people like walking in parks because the environment is more pleasant. There’s more fresh air and greenery, which helps people relax and escape from the noise of the city for a while.

questions.text: Where would you like to take a long walk if you had the chance?
questions.answer: If I had the chance, I’d like to take a long walk along the seaside or by a river. I enjoy places where I can walk at my own pace and enjoy the view without feeling rushed.

questions.text: Where did you go for a walk lately?
questions.answer: Lately, I’ve been taking walks around my neighbourhood. There’s a small park nearby, and I sometimes go there in the evening to stretch my legs and unwind after a busy day.

topics.title: Hobbies

questions.text: Do you have any hobbies?
questions.answer: Yes, I do. In my free time, I enjoy doing a few simple things, like listening to music and watching shows. These hobbies help me relax and take my mind off work.

questions.text: Did you have any hobbies when you were a child?
questions.answer: Yes, I did. When I was a child, I liked playing outside with friends and watching cartoons. I didn’t really call them hobbies back then, but I spent a lot of time

questions.text: doing those things 3. Do you have a hobby that you’ve had since childhood?
questions.answer: Yes, I do. I’ve enjoyed listening to music since I was young. Even though my taste in music has changed over time, listening to music has always been a part of my daily life.

questions.text: Do you have the same hobbies as your family members?
questions.answer: Some of them are the same, but not all. For example, my family members and I all enjoy watching TV together, but we also have our own interests. I think that’s quite normal in most families.

topics.title: Dreams

questions.text: Can you remember the dreams you had?
questions.answer: Sometimes I can, but not very clearly. I usually remember my dreams right after I wake up, but they fade quite quickly. After a while, I can only remember a few random scenes.

questions.text: Do you share your dreams with others?
questions.answer: Not very often. I only share my dreams with close friends if they ’ re interesting really make much sense.

questions.text: Do you think dreams have special meanings?
questions.answer: I’m not completely sure, but I think dreams can sometimes reflect our feelings or stress in real life. I don’t believe every dream has a special meaning, but some of them might be connected to what we’re experiencing.

questions.text: Do you want to make your dreams come true?
questions.answer: Yes, of course. I think having dreams gives people motivation and direction. Even if not all of them come true, working towards them can still be meaningful and rewarding.

topics.title: Typing

questions.text: Do you prefer typing or handwriting?
questions.answer: To be honest, it depends on the occasion! For study and work—like writing essays or taking notes—I prefer typing because it’s faster and easier to edit. But for personal stuff, like writing cards or a journal, I love handwriting. It feels more personal and helps me remember things better. I use both, but each has its own place!

questions.text: Do you type on a desktop or laptop keyboard?
questions.answer: I mostly use a laptop keyboard! It’s portable, so I can type anywhere—class, library, or even when I’m out. At home, I sometimes use a desktop keyboard because it’s more comfortable for long typing sessions, like writing essays. But overall, my laptop keyboard is my main choice.

questions.text: When did you learn how to type on a keyboard?
questions.answer: I learned to type properly at around 12, in junior high computer class. My teacher showed me the right finger positions, and I practiced daily with typing software. At first I was slow, but now I can touch-type without looking. It’s a really handy skill for my schoolwork!

questions.text: How do you improve your typing?
questions.answer: I improve my typing with daily practice and good habits! I use typing apps for 10 minutes a day to build muscle memory for touch-typing, and I always stick to correct finger positions in daily use, no matter how slow I am. I also keep a good posture to avoid tiredness. These simple steps have made my typing much faster and more accurate!

topics.title: Childhood activities

questions.text: What were your favourite activities when you were a child?
questions.answer: When I was a child, I loved two things most: playing outdoors with friends and reading storybooks! We played hide-and-seek and tag in the park after school, and I read fairy tales every night before bed. Those were such carefree, fun days, and I still miss those simple, happy moments a lot!

questions.text: Did you prefer to do activities alone or with a group of people when you were a child?
questions.answer: When I was a kid, I mostly loved group activities! I was energetic and loved playing outdoor games with friends, like hide-and-seek and tag. But I also enjoyed quiet alone time, reading or drawing in my room. Both were fun—group play for excitement, alone time for peace!

topics.title: Buildings

questions.text: Do you take photos of buildings?
questions.answer: Not really, but I do take photos of buildings occasionally! I love vintage and historic buildings with unique details, like old townhouses or European-style landmarks. I usually snap shots when I’m traveling or walking in old districts, to capture their charm and keep memories of the places I visit.

questions.text: Is there a building that you would like to visit?
questions.answer: Yes, I’ve always wanted to visit the Eiffel Tower in Paris! It’s such an iconic landmark with a unique iron design. I’d love to climb up for panoramic views of the city, take sunset photos, and feel the romantic vibe. It’s been on my bucket list for years, and I hope to go there soon!

questions.text: Are there tall buildings near your home？
questions.answer: Yes, there are several tall buildings near my home! There are two residential high-rises across the street and a modern office skyscraper nearby with a shopping mall below. They’re super convenient—with cafes and shops on the ground floors—and they make the area look lively at night.

topics.title: Views

questions.text: Do you like taking pictures of different views?
questions.answer: Absolutely, I love taking photos of different views! I enjoy shooting natural scenery like mountains and sunsets, as well as urban views like city skylines and old streets. I take photos when I travel or walk around, and it helps me capture memories and notice beautiful details I’d otherwise miss. It’s a really lovely hobby!

questions.text: Do you prefer views in urban areas or rural areas?
questions.answer: It depends on my mood! For excitement, I love urban views—like the glittering city skyline and historic streets. But when I want to relax, I prefer rural scenery, with green fields, quiet lanes and starry skies. Both are amazing, just for different vibes!

questions.text: Do you prefer views in your own country or in other countries?
questions.answer: It’s hard to choose! I love my country’s diverse views—snowy mountains, green terraces and ancient towns with rich culture, which feel warm and familiar. But I’m also drawn to exotic foreign views like tropical beaches and European castles—they’re fresh and eye-opening. I cherish both for different reasons!

topics.title: Scenery

questions.text: Do you look out the window at the scenery when travelling by bus or car?
questions.answer: Absolutely, I love looking out the window when travelling! On long trips, I’ll gaze at the scenery instead of using my phone—green fields, villages, or city streets. It’s relaxing, and I often spot beautiful little things like sunflower fields or sunsets that make the journey more enjoyable.

questions.text: Do you prefer the mountains or the sea?
questions.answer: I slightly prefer the mountains, but I love the sea too! Mountains are great for hiking—fresh air, forest views and peak panoramas make me feel calm and free from city stress. The sea is perfect for relaxing: beach walks, wave sounds and sunsets are so soothing. Both are amazing, just for different moods!

questions.text: Do you like to take scenery pictures?
questions.answer: Absolutely, I love taking scenery pictures! I enjoy shooting natural views like mountains, lakes and sunsets, as well as urban scenery like city skylines and old streets. I take photos when I travel or walk around, and it helps me capture memories and notice beautiful details I’d otherwise miss. It’s a really lovely hobby!

questions.text: What are the most beautiful sights you have seen while travelling?
questions.answer: The most beautiful sights I’ve seen are the sea of clouds at Huangshan and the sunset over Erhai Lake! At Huangshan, clouds surrounded the peaks like a fairyland at dawn. In Dali, the sunset turned Erhai Lake golden and pink, which was so peaceful. Both were absolutely stunning and left me with unforgettable memories!

topics.title: Describe a family member who you are proud of.

what she/he has done to make you feel proud

part3.text: When was the last time that you felt proud of yourself ?
part3.answer: The last time I felt proud of myself was when I managed to overcome a personal challenge that required long-term effort. It wasn’t something dramatic, but it took a lot of self-discipline and persistence. Looking back, what made me proud wasn’t the final result, but the fact that I stayed committed even when progress was slow. In my opinion, being able to push through difficulties and stay responsible for one’s own goals is something worth feeling proud of.

part3.text: What would children do to make their parents proud ?
part3.answer: In general, children can make their parents proud by showing responsibility and independence. This doesn’t necessarily mean achieving outstanding academic results. In many cases, parents care more about their children’s attitude, such as being honest, hardworking, and willing to take responsibility for their actions. When children show respect to others and make sensible decisions, parents are more likely to feel proud of them.

part3.text: What did you to make your parents proud when you were young ?
part3.answer: When I was young, the main thing I did to make my parents proud was trying to behave well and take school seriously. I followed rules, completed my homework on time, and didn’t cause them much trouble. Although these actions may seem ordinary, they showed that I was responsible for my role as a student. From my parents’ perspective, consistency and good behaviour were more important than short-term achievements.

part3.text: What advantages of yours make you proud?
part3.answer: One advantage that makes me feel proud is my ability to stay calm under pressure. In many situations, instead of panicking, I tend to analyse the problem and look for practical solutions. This helps me deal with challenges more effectively, both in work and in daily life. I believe this quality has been developed over time, and it allows me to handle responsibilities with more confidence.

topics.answer: I’d like to talk about my mother, who is the family member I feel most proud of. She has always played an important role in my life, not only as a parent but also as someone I truly respect. We don’t spend time together every day because we’re both busy, but we usually see each other on weekends or during family gatherings. Even when we’re not together, we stay in touch through phone calls and messages. What makes me feel proud of her is her attitude towards life. She has faced many difficulties, especially balancing work and family, but she never complains. Instead, she always stays calm and tries to solve problems step by step. She has also been very supportive of my choices, even when they were not the easiest or safest ones. I’m proud of her because she sets a good example for me. She shows me what responsibility, patience, and resilience really mean. Her actions have influenced the way I deal with challenges in my own life.

topics.title: Describe a famous person you would like to meet

part3.text: What are the advantages and disadvantages of being a famous child ?
part3.answer: In general, being a famous child has both advantages and disadvantages. On the positive side, famous children often have access to better resources, such as professional training and financial support, which can help them develop their skills more quickly. However, there are also clear downsides. They may face heavy pressure from public expectations and lose their privacy at a very young age. This can affect their emotional development and mental health in the long run.

part3.text: What can today’s children do to become famous?
part3.answer: Nowadays, children have more ways to become famous than in the past. Many of them use social media platforms to share their talents, such as singing, dancing, or creating videos. In addition, some children gain attention through competitions or talent shows. However, becoming famous often requires not only ability, but also guidance from adults and responsible management, especially at a young age.

part3.text: What can children do with their fame?
part3.answer: If managed properly, children can use their fame in positive ways. For example, they can inspire others by setting a good example or raise awareness about meaningful social issues. At the same time, it is important that their fame does not interfere with their education or normal childhood. Fame should be treated as a tool, not the main goal of their development.

part3.text: Do people become famous because of their talent ?
part3.answer: Talent is certainly an important factor, but it is not the only reason people become famous. In many cases, timing, opportunity, and media exposure also play a significant role. Some people become famous because they meet public demand at the right moment, even if their talent is not exceptional. Therefore, fame is often the result of a combination of talent and external factors.

topics.answer: I’d like to talk about a famous person I would like to meet, who is Jack Ma, the founder of Alibaba. He is well known in China and around the world as a successful entrepreneur. I first learned about him through news reports and interviews many years ago, especially when Alibaba was growing rapidly. What impressed me most was not only his business success, but also the way he talked about failure and perseverance. If I had the chance, I would like to meet him at a public talk or a small seminar rather than a formal business setting. I think that kind of environment would allow for more relaxed and meaningful communication. I would like to meet him because his life experience is very inspiring. He failed many times before becoming successful, but he never gave up. I believe talking to someone like him would help me gain a different perspective on success and personal growth.

part3.text: Do you think it’s important to plan ahead?
part3.answer: Yes, I believe planning ahead is important in many aspects of life. It helps people set clear goals, manage their time more efficiently, and reduce uncertainty. When people plan in advance, they are more likely to make rational decisions and avoid unnecessary stress. However, flexibility is also essential, as unexpected situations can always arise.

part3.text: Do you think children should plan their future careers?
part3.answer: I think children can start thinking about their future careers, but detailed planning may be too early. At a young age, children are still exploring their interests and abilities. Instead of fixed career plans, they should focus on developing skills, gaining experience, and understanding different possibilities. Career planning can become more specific as they grow older.

part3.text: Should children ask their teachers or parents for advice when making plans ?
part3.answer: Yes, I think seeking advice from teachers and parents is very helpful. Teachers can provide guidance based on education and academic performance, while parents often offer practical advice based on life experience. However, children should also be encouraged to think independently and make final decisions that suit their own goals and personalities.

part3.text: What is the right age for a child to learn drawing?
part3.answer: I believe there is no fixed right age, but early childhood is a suitable time to start. Young children naturally enjoy drawing as a form of play and self-expression. At this stage, learning should focus on creativity rather than technique. Formal training can be introduced gradually as children grow older and develop better control and concentration.

part3.text: Why do most children draw more often than adults do?
part3.answer: One reason is that children have fewer responsibilities and more free time. More importantly, children are less afraid of making mistakes and being judged. For them, drawing is a natural way to express emotions and imagination. In contrast, adults often focus on practicality and results, which may reduce their willingness to draw freely.

part3.text: Why do some people visit galleries or museums instead of viewing artworks online?
part3.answer: Visiting galleries or museums offers a more immersive experience. People can see the real size, texture, and details of artworks, which are often lost online. In addition, the atmosphere of these places allows visitors to focus and reflect more deeply, creating a stronger emotional connection with the artworks.

part3.text: Do you think galleries and museums should be free of change?
part3.answer: I think it depends on the situation. Free entry can make art more accessible to the public and encourage cultural education. However, museums also need funding to maintain collections and improve services. A balanced approach, such as free days or discounted tickets for students, may be a practical solution.

part3.text: How do artworks inspire people?
part3.answer: Artworks can inspire people by offering new perspectives and emotional experiences. They may encourage viewers to reflect on life, society, or personal values. In some cases, art also stimulates creativity and motivates people to express themselves in different ways, whether through art or other forms.

topics.answer: I’d like to talk about a child I know who is very fond of drawing. He is my cousin’s son, and I got to know him quite well through family gatherings. He is a quiet and patient child, and he often prefers staying alone rather than playing noisy games. He is quite observant and tends to notice small details in his surroundings, which I think is closely related to his interest in drawing. He draws almost every day, especially after school or during weekends. Sometimes he can sit quietly for over an hour just focusing on his drawings. He usually draws animals, cartoons, and scenes from his daily life.I think he likes drawing because it allows him to express himself freely. Drawing helps him relax and turn his imagination into something visible. It also gives him a sense of achievement when he finishes a piece of work.

part3.text: Do you think children are born smart or they learn to become smart?
part3.answer: I believe it’s both nature and nurture! Kids are born with some innate intellectual potential—some have a natural knack for learning faster or remembering things better. But this is just a starting point. What makes children truly smart is the environment: supportive parents, good education, and chances to explore and think critically. A child with average innate ability can become very intelligent with the right learning opportunities. So innate talent matters, but learning and experience are far more decisive.

part3.text: How do children become smart at school?
part3.answer: I think children get smarter at school through interactive learning, hands-on activities and peer collaboration, not just textbook memorization. First, teachers use discussions and open questions to encourage critical thinking, instead of just lecturing. Second, schools offer experiments and projects that let kids apply knowledge, deepening their understanding. Third, working with classmates exposes them to new ideas, helping them learn from each other. Good teachers also give personalized support, nurturing curiosity—this is what really develops children’s intelligence at school.

part3.text: Why are some people well-rounded and others only good at one thing?
part3.answer: I think it’s a combination of education, personal choice, talent and resources that makes some people well-rounded and others specialized. First, early education matters: those with holistic learning, trying sports, arts and academics, become versatile, while others are pushed to focus on one skill from childhood. Second, personal interest and talent play a role—some love exploring new things, while others have a strong innate gift in one area and choose to delve deep. Resource constraints also matter: not everyone can access diverse learning opportunities, limiting their ability to develop multiple skills. Both paths are valuable in different situations.

part3.text: Why does modern society need talents of all kinds?
part3.answer: Modern society needs all kinds of talents because it’s complex, highly specialized and has diverse needs. First, every industry—tech, medicine, art, education—relies on its own skilled experts; none can be replaced. Second, big problems like climate change or public health need cross-disciplinary teamwork, not just single specialists. Also, diverse talents spark innovation: mixing tech and art, business and social work creates new ideas. So all types of talents work together to keep society running and moving forward.

topics.answer: I’d like to talk about Lily, the former president of my university’s English Debate Society, who solved a recruitment problem in a really smart way last semester. Lily didn’t panic; she figured out freshmen loved short videos and interactive activities, so she made a clever plan. First, she had us film 3 funny short videos about debate life and trendy topics, posting them on campus social media—they got thousands of views quickly. Second, she organized flash debates at the canteen and library, drawing crowds and handing out QR code flyers for our recruitment group. Third, she partnered with campus shops: freshmen joining the group got small discounts, which brought in more sign-ups. She even adjusted our content hourly based on data to make it more effective. She understood the audience and used resources wisely, which made the solution both creative and practical.

part3.text: What things do families keep for a long time?
part3.answer: Families keep many long-term items, mainly those with sentimental or historical value. First, heirlooms like vintage jewelry, antique furniture or traditional crafts are passed down, symbolizing family heritage. Second, memorabilia such as old photo albums, letters or diaries are treasured, as they capture precious family moments. Also, practical items with stories—like a grandma’s sewing machine or dad’s tools—are kept, carrying family love and craftsmanship. Some also preserve cultural items like family trees or traditional costumes to keep traditions alive.

part3.text: What's the difference between things valued by people in the past and today?
part3.answer: The main difference is that past people valued tangible, practical and traditional items, while today we focus more on intangible experiences and personalized things. In the past, material scarcity made durable, functional objects like handcrafted furniture, farming tools or family heirlooms precious—they were useful and carried cultural/family stories. Now, we value experiences like travel or concerts, digital assets like cloud-stored memories, and personalized items for self-expression. Emotional value still counts, but we care less about physical durability and more about personal growth and memorable moments.

part3.text: What kinds of things are kept in museums?
part3.answer: Museums keep various items, mainly archaeological artifacts, art masterpieces, natural specimens, tech exhibits and folk cultural relics. Archaeological pieces like ancient pottery, bronze and scrolls reveal past human life. Art works include paintings, sculptures and calligraphy, reflecting human creativity. Natural specimens such as dinosaur fossils and minerals teach us about Earth’s history. Tech exhibits track scientific progress, from ancient inventions to modern prototypes. Folk relics like traditional costumes preserve local culture and heritage.

part3.text: What's the influence of technology on museums？
part3.answer: I think technology has greatly improved museums in three key ways. First, digital tools like 3D scanning and virtual exhibitions let visitors see relics in detail and access museums online, breaking geographic limits. Second, AR/VR and interactive screens create immersive experiences, making museums more fun for young people. Third, high-tech conservation methods protect fragile relics from damage, extending their life. Overall, technology makes museums more accessible, engaging and better at preserving heritage.

topics.answer: I’d like to talk about a vintage brass pocket watch, a family heirloom passed down for nearly 90 years. It’s a small, elegant timepiece with my great-grandfather’s initials carved on the back, and it still works perfectly after all these years. My family has had it since the early 1930s. My great-grandfather, a watchmaker in Shanghai, handcrafted it himself over three months as a coming-of-age gift for my grandfather. Later, it was passed to my father as a wedding gift, and last year, my father gave it to me on my 20th birthday. It’s important to my family for three reasons. First, it’s a symbol of family heritage, witnessing nearly a century of our history and carrying stories of three generations. Second, it embodies my great-grandfather’s craftsmanship and values—meticulousness and dedication, which remind us to pursue excellence in everything we do. Third, it has deep emotional meaning, connecting me to my ancestors and serving as a spiritual bond for our family. Its sentimental value is far greater than any monetary worth, making it the most precious thing in our family.

part3.answer: Children often want to do jobs that they find exciting or admirable. Common examples include doctors, teachers, police officers, athletes, and entertainers. part3.text: What should people consider when choosing jobs?
part3.answer: When choosing a job, people should consider several factors, including personal interests, skills, work-life balance, and long-term career prospects. Job satisfaction often depends on whether the work aligns with a person’ s values and strengths. Practical factors such as job stability and working environment should also be taken into account.

part3.text: Is salary the main reason people choose a certain job?
part3.answer: Salary is an important factor, but it is not always the main reason. While financial security is necessary, many people also value job satisfaction, personal growth, and a sense of achievement. In the long run, a job that offers meaning and balance may be more sustainable than one that is only well-paid.

part3.text: Do people's ideal jobs change as they grow up?
part3.answer: Definitely, people’s ideal jobs change a lot as they grow up, because our priorities and understanding of work shift with age. As kids, we dream of glamorous jobs like astronauts or pop stars, drawn to fantasy and excitement with no idea of the hard work involved. As teenagers, we aim for stable, respected careers like doctors or engineers, influenced by family and social expectations. As adults, we care more about work-life balance, personal fulfillment and purpose, not just salary or status. For example, I once wanted to be a celebrity, but now I prefer a quiet job in education that lets me help others. So ideal jobs evolve with our maturity and life experience.

part3.text: What are the factors that make a successful movie?
part3.answer: I think five key factors make a movie successful: a compelling story, high production values, smart marketing, audience resonance, and a talented team. First, a tight plot, deep characters and meaningful themes are the foundation—without a good story, effects are meaningless. Second, stunning visuals, sound and VFX elevate the experience, especially for sci-fi/epic films. Third, strategic marketing (ads, premieres) and timely release (festive seasons) build hype and maximize viewers. Fourth, the movie must resonate emotionally/culturally, reflecting audience values or daily life. Finally, a skilled director, talented actors and professional crew bring the story to life. Success needs all factors working together, not just one.

part3.text: Do Chinese people prefer to watch domestic movies or foreian movies?

Foreign films dominate hard sci-fi, superheroes and thrillers, offering spectacular visuals and exotic adventure that Chinese cinema still lacks in some niche areas. Older people favor domestic films for cultural relevance, while young people watch both, choosing by quality/genre. part3.text: Why do people laugh in their daily lives?
part3.answer: People laugh in their daily lives mainly because laughter is a natural way to express positive emotions such as happiness, relief, or amusement. It helps people respond to humorous situations and makes daily interactions more enjoyable. In addition, laughter often works as a social signal. When people laugh together, it shows friendliness and openness, which can reduce tension and make communication smoother. In this sense, laughter is not only about humor but also about maintaining healthy social relationships.

part3.text: Do you think people laugh less now than in the past? Why or why not?
part3.answer: I believe people may laugh less in certain situations today compared with the past, mainly due to increased stress in modern life. Fast-paced work environments and heavy responsibilities can reduce opportunities for relaxed social interactions. However, on the other hand, people now have more access to entertainment through social media, videos, and online content. These platforms provide new ways for people to experience humor. So while the form of laughter may have changed, it does not necessarily mean that people laugh significantly less overall.

part3.text: How does laughter help people to connect with each other?
part3.answer: Laughter helps people connect by creating a sense of shared experience. When people laugh together, they feel emotionally closer and more comfortable with each other. Moreover, laughter can break down social barriers. It reduces awkwardness, especially among strangers, and makes communication feel more natural. In many cases, people who laugh together are more likely to trust each other, which strengthens both personal and professional relationships.

part3.text: In what situations is laughter considered inappropriate in your culture?

People are expected to show understanding and emotional sensitivity rather than humor in such situations.

part3.text: Do you think air pollution comes mostly from mobile vehicles?

part3.text: Do you think people need to change the way of transportation drastically to protect the environment?

part3.text: How are the transportation systems in urban areas and rural areas different?
part3.answer: Transportation systems in urban areas are usually more developed and diverse. part3.text: How can leaders encourage their employees?
part3.answer: Leaders can encourage employees in six key ways: specific recognition, empowerment, growth support, positive culture, fair incentives, and genuine communication. First, give specific, timely praise for exact contributions (not empty “good job”) to make employees feel valued. Second, empower staff with autonomy and delegation—trust them to make decisions, fostering ownership. Third, provide growth opportunities like training, promotions or rotations, so employees see a future. Fourth, build a positive culture that tolerates mistakes and rewards innovation, boosting morale. Fifth, use fair incentives (bonuses, flexible hours) to reward effort fairly. Finally, communicate openly—listen to employees’ concerns to build loyalty. All these make employees feel trusted and motivated to perform well.

part3.text: When should parents encourage their children?
part3.answer: Parents should encourage their children at five key times: when trying new things, facing failure, lacking confidence, making small progress, or making choices. First, when kids try new things (like first swimming lessons), encouragement helps them overcome fear and take the first step. Second, when they fail (bad exam, lost game), encouragement teaches resilience instead of making them feel ashamed. Third, when they doubt themselves (shy to speak, think they’re not good enough), affirmation builds self-worth. Fourth, celebrating small progress (finishing homework, practicing piano) reinforces good habits. Finally, when choosing hobbies/subjects, encouraging independent choice builds autonomy. These moments need support most—encouragement shapes confidence and resilience, not just praise for success.

part3.text: What kind of encouragement should parents give?
part3.answer: Parents should give specific, effort-focused, empathetic, empowering and boundary-setting encouragement, not empty praise or overindulgence. First, specific praise (highlighting exact efforts like “you practiced piano daily and improved a lot”) makes kids feel valued, unlike vague “good job.” Second, focus on effort over talent—praise persistence, not just results, to build a growth mindset and resilience. Third, empathetic encouragement validates kids’ feelings first (e.g., “I know you’re scared”) before motivating them, building trust. Fourth, empowering encouragement supports independence (trying new things) with safety, not pressure. Finally, encourage with clear boundaries to teach responsibility, avoiding spoiling. This sincere, growth-focused encouragement builds real confidence and character.

part3.text: Do you think some people are better than othersat persuading?
part3.answer: Yes, some people are definitely better at persuading others—this comes from a mix of natural traits, learned skills, empathy and credibility. First, charismatic, confident and articulate people have a natural edge, as they project trust and conviction. Second, skilled persuaders use active listening to tailor messages to others’ needs, and back arguments with evidence/logic, not empty claims. Third, high EQ and empathy let them validate others’ feelings first, building trust and reducing resistance. Fourth, credibility (expertise, honesty) makes their words more believable. Finally, adaptability—adjusting style for different audiences—boosts effectiveness. While persuasion can be learned, these factors make some people naturally better at it.

topics.answer: I’d like to talk about encouraging my best friend Lily to join the Campus English Speech Contest last month. At first, she reacted very negatively: she shook her head, frowned, and said she’d forget lines, stutter, and make a fool of herself. Her voice trembled, and she tried to avoid the topic, clearly scared of stage fright. I encouraged her for three reasons. First, I didn’t want her talent to go to waste—she’s capable but hides it due to anxiety. Second, public speaking is crucial for her future study abroad (she wants to go to the UK), helping her with interviews and presentations. Third, I wanted to support her as she’d supported me before, pushing her to break her comfort zone. I helped her draft the speech, practiced with her daily, and taught her breathing exercises to calm nerves. She finally agreed, and on the contest day, she delivered it perfectly and won second prize! Now she’s much more confident, even hosting English corner. I encouraged her to help her discover her strength and grow, not just for a prize.

part3.text: Do you think adults can have lots of imagination?
part3.answer: Yes, adults absolutely can have rich imagination—even more sophisticated and purposeful than children’s, though it shows in different ways. Adult imagination drives innovation and problem-solving: sci-fi authors create epic worlds, engineers design futuristic tech, and designers craft unique spaces—all using experience-based, practical creativity. Many adults also nurture imagination through hobbies: writing novels, painting, or planning themed trips, finding fulfillment in creative thinking. Adults’ imagination balances creativity with reality, making it actionable. While some lose touch due to busy routines, it’s dormant, not gone—easily reawakened with creative activities. Adult imagination is mature, purposeful, and the engine of innovation and personal growth.

part3.text: Do you think imagination is essential for scientists?
part3.answer: Yes, imagination is absolutely essential for scientists—it’s the driving force behind all major scientific breakthroughs, complementing logic and experimentation. First, imagination is key to forming hypotheses: Einstein imagined riding a light beam to develop relativity, Darwin imagined natural selection before finding full evidence—no imagination, no meaningful theories. Second, it fuels innovative experiment design: Watson and Crick imagined DNA’s double helix via model-building, a creative approach no one used before. Third, imagination lets scientists break old paradigms—Copernicus imagined heliocentrism to challenge geocentrism, quantum mechanics came from imagining a weird microscopic world. Fourth, it drives real-world applications: Faraday imagined electricity’s practical use, leading to generators. Scientific imagination is grounded in knowledge, not fantasy, and is the soul of scientific progress.

part3.text: What kinds of jobs need imagination?
part3.answer: Imagination is essential for creative arts, science/tech innovation, education/communication, experience services, and entrepreneurial jobs—roles that need original ideas, not just routine tasks. Creative jobs (writers, designers, filmmakers) build unique worlds/visuals; science/tech jobs (scientists, engineers) imagine new theories/tech to solve problems. Education/communication jobs (teachers, marketers) use imagination to make lessons/campaigns engaging. Experience jobs (chefs, event planners) craft unique experiences, and entrepreneurial jobs need imagination to envision new business models. All these roles rely on imagination to create something original and impactful.

part3.text: What subjects are helpful for children's imagination?
part3.answer: Literature, visual arts, science, history, and performing arts are the most helpful subjects for children’s imagination—each stimulates creativity in unique ways. First, literature (fairy tales, fantasy stories) lets kids imagine characters, worlds and plots, and creative writing turns them into active creators. Second, visual arts (drawing, craft) let kids visualize ideas into tangible art, with no strict rules. Third, science sparks “what if” questions and simple experiments, blending creativity with problem-solving. Fourth, history lets kids imagine ancient life and cultures via role-play, expanding horizons. Fifth, performing arts (drama, music) encourage role-play and improvisation, turning imagination into interactive fun. Cross-disciplinary learning (art+science) boosts it further—all these subjects nurture creative thinking beyond rote learning.

part3.text: What games help develop children's imagination?
part3.answer: Open-ended, creative games best develop children’s imagination—including pretend role-play, constructive building, art & craft, outdoor exploration, and collaborative storytelling games. First, pretend play (pirates, doctors, wizards) lets kids invent characters, settings and plots from scratch, the most direct imagination booster. Second, building games (Lego, blocks) let them imagine and construct castles, future cities or secret hideouts, making imagination tangible. Third, art & craft (drawing, clay) lets kids visualize whimsical creatures/magical scenes with no rules. Fourth, outdoor games (treasure hunts, nature quests) use nature as a canvas for imaginary adventures. Fifth, storytelling games (story chains) spark collective imagination. These child-led, unstructured games let imagination thrive, unlike rule-bound competitive games.

part3.text: How important is imagination to children?
part3.answer: Yes, imagination is extremely important and foundational for children—it drives their cognitive growth, emotional development, social skills and creative potential, far beyond just being fun. First, it helps kids learn abstract concepts (math, science) by turning them into vivid mental images, and fuels curiosity to explore the world. Second, it’s the bedrock of creative thinking—kids draw, build, write original ideas, building innovation for problem-solving later. Third, pretend play fosters empathy and emotional intelligence, as kids imagine others’ feelings. Fourth, group imaginative play teaches teamwork and communication, boosting social skills. Fifth, it builds resilience—imagining positive outcomes helps kids cope with setbacks and stay positive. Nurtured imagination shapes holistic growth, making it indispensable for children.

topics.answer: I’d like to talk about using my imagination for my university Creative Writing class’s final sci-fi short story assignment last month. I worked on it in the campus library for three evenings. I needed imagination because the task was totally open-ended—no given plots, characters or settings. I had to build a future world from scratch: create a city, design characters, and craft an original plot, with no real-life references to rely on. At first, it was extremely hard—I had a blank mind, felt stuck and doubted my creativity. But after a break, I got the idea of a “Memory Restorer” in a future city where people store memories in chips. This sparked my imagination, and drafting became easy as I let ideas flow (glowing memory chips, floating skyscrapers, a mystery about the main character’s lost memory). After finishing, I felt proud, excited and surprised—proud to overcome the block, excited about the story I built, and surprised to find I had more imagination than I thought. It taught me imagination is a learnable skill, not just a gift, and I felt fulfilled creating something original and meaningful.

part3.text: What kind of music events do people like today?
part3.answer: People today love immersive, personalized, cross-border, community-focused and tech-integrated music events, far beyond traditional stadium concerts. First, immersive live experiences (livehouse shows, outdoor festivals like Strawberry) let fans get close to artists, with a free, carnival vibe—turning music into a social adventure. Second, niche/personalized events (indie showcases, genre-specific festivals, cultural music salons) cater to specific tastes, unlike generic mainstream shows. Third, cross-border events (music+art, music+VR, music+tourism) offer fresh, multi-sensory experiences. Fourth, community/theme events (charity concerts, retro music nights) build belonging and shared emotion. Fifth, online-offline integrated events (live-streamed concerts, hybrid festivals) make music accessible to all. While big stadium shows still exist, modern audiences prioritize experience, personalization and connection over scale.

part3.text: Do you think children should receive some music a education?
part3.answer: Yes, children absolutely should receive music education—it’s essential for their holistic development, nurturing cognitive skills, emotional intelligence, creativity, social competence and aesthetic literacy. First, music boosts cognitive growth: learning rhythm, notation and coordination enhances concentration, memory, and even math/language skills. Second, it fosters emotional intelligence: music conveys feelings, helping kids identify and regulate emotions, and build empathy. Third, it ignites creativity and imagination: kids improvise melodies, write lyrics or adapt songs, turning listening into active creation. Fourth, group music activities (choir, band) teach teamwork and communication, building social skills and confidence. Fifth, it cultivates aesthetic and cultural awareness: diverse music genres expose kids to beauty and global cultures. Music education should be playful, not exam-focused—its goal is to nurture a lifelong love of music, not just technical skills, making it indispensable for children’s well-rounded growth.

part3.text: What are the differences between old and you no people's music preferences?
part3.answer: Old and young people have striking differences in music preferences—rooted in generational experiences, emotional needs and lifestyle. First, genre: Young people love modern, trendy genres (pop, EDM, rap, ACG) for novelty and self-expression; older adults prefer classic oldies, folk music, opera—familiar, nostalgic genres tied to their youth and culture, finding modern music jarring. Second, theme/emotion: Young people listen for self-expression, emotional release and social bonding (songs about youth/love); older adults seek comfort, nostalgia and cultural connection (classic songs evoking memories, traditional values). Third, listening habits: Young people love social, immersive live events (festivals, livehouses); older adults prefer quiet, low-key listening (radio, park folk shows) to avoid loud chaos. Fourth, role in life: Young people use music as a social identity and daily companion; older adults see it as a leisure comfort and emotional anchor. While some overlap exists, generational differences remain stark.

part3.text: What kind of music events are there in your country?
part3.answer: In my country, there are diverse music events—large commercial concerts, outdoor festivals, livehouse shows, traditional folk/opera events, campus activities, online-offline integrated events, and niche theme-based gatherings. First, large stadium concerts (for Jay Chou, Taylor Swift) are mainstream, with spectacular stages and huge crowds. Second, outdoor festivals (Strawberry, Midi) offer indie, rock, folk, electronic music with a carnival vibe, popular with young people. Third, livehouse gigs (small venues) host indie/folk artists, letting fans get close to performers. Fourth, traditional events (Guoyue salons, Peking Opera shows) preserve cultural heritage, popular with elders and Hanfu fans. Fifth, campus activities (singer contests, welcome parties) are student-led and inclusive. Sixth, online cloud concerts (post-pandemic) reach global fans. Finally, niche events (ACG music, retro nights, jazz clubs) cater to specific tastes. All blend Chinese culture with modern trends, making the music scene vibrant and diverse.

topics.answer: I’d like to talk about the university Freshmen Welcome Party I attended last month, where I hated the music played. I went with my roommate Lily, to the school’s main auditorium on Friday evening. I decided to go because it was a key freshmen event—I wanted to make new friends, break the ice, and immerse myself in campus life. But I absolutely didn’t enjoy the music, for four reasons: First, wrong genre—non-stop loud EDM with heavy bass, instead of warm folk/pop, clashing with the welcome party’s friendly vibe. Second, ear-splitting volume—it vibrated the auditorium, made my ears ring and head throb, drowning out all conversation and hosts’ words. Third, chaotic structure—random tracks with jarring transitions, no match for performances (e.g., loud EDM during a poetry recital, ruining the moment). Fourth, no emotional connection—generic club music, no campus spirit or new-beginning vibe, soulless and irrelevant. I was so uncomfortable that Lily and I left early, with a headache and ringing ears. The music was mismatched, painful, chaotic and soulless—it ruined the whole welcome party, and I was totally disappointed.

topics.answer: I’d like to talk about Joy City, a popular shopping mall in the city center of Chengdu, right next to Line 1 metro and Tianfu Square. I don’t have to go to different places, saving lots of time. Second, the environment is comfortable—clean, well-lit, with air conditioning and rest areas, plus cafes for breaks. It makes shopping relaxing, not tiring. Third, the service is great: friendly staff, easy returns and exchanges at the customer service desk. Also, it has restaurants, a cinema and a kids’ area, so we can combine shopping with dining or entertainment. It’s convenient and enjoyable, which is why I love shopping here.

topics.title: Plants

questions.text: Do you keep plants at home?
questions.answer: Yeah, I do! I have a couple of small plants on my desk and a bigger one in the living room. They make the place feel fresher and more welcoming.

questions.text: What plant did you grow when you were young?
questions.answer: When I was a kid, I grew some sunflowers in the backyard. They grew really tall, and I remember feeling proud when they finally bloomed. It was a fun little project.

questions.text: Do you know anything about growing a plant?
questions.answer: I know a little bit, like making sure the plant gets enough sunlight and water. It’s also important not to overwater it. Other than that, I just try to keep it healthy.

questions.text: Do Chinese people send plants as a gift to other people?
questions.answer: Yes, they do. People often give plants like orchids or lucky bamboo because they symbolize good fortune. It’s a thoughtful gift, especially for new homes or business openings.

topics.title: Public places

questions.text: Have you ever talked with someone you don’t know in public places?
questions.answer: Yeah, I have—once I was waiting for the bus on a rainy day, and an older lady next to me struck up a conversation about the weather; we ended up chatting for 10 minutes, and it made the wait feel way shorter.Another time, I had to ask a stranger in a café to pass me the sugar since it was on their side of the table, and we even exchanged a few words about how busy the place was that morning.

questions.text: Do you wear headphones in public places?
questions.answer: Yeah, I usually wear headphones when I’m out in public—like on the subway or walking to class—because they help me drown out the noise and let me focus on my music or podcasts.I don’t crank the volume up too high, though; I make sure I can still hear a bit of what’s going on around me, just so I don’t zone out completely and miss things like my subway stop.

topics.title: Rules

questions.text: Are there any rules for students at your school?
questions.answer: Yeah, there are a few basic rules at my school—like we’ve gotta show up to class on time every morning, cause if you’re late too often, you might get a warning from the teacher. We also can’t eat or drink in the classrooms, only in the cafeteria—they say it helps keep the learning space neat.

questions.text: Do you think students would benefit more from rules?
questions.answer: Yeah, I definitely think students get more benefits from rules—they help keep things organized, so we don’t end up in chaos, and they also teach us to stick to a routine, which is super useful for later life. Without clear rules, it’d be easy for people to skip homework or disrupt classes, so having them actually creates a fair environment where everyone can focus on learning without distractions.

questions.text: Do you have a teacher who does his/her job very well?
questions.answer: Yeah, definitely—my math teacher is awesome at her job; she always breaks down tough concepts into simple parts so even students who struggle with math can keep up, and she’s super patient when we ask questions.She also goes the extra mile to help us outside class, like staying after school to review tricky topics—you can tell she really cares about our progress, which makes everyone want to work harder.

topics.title: Shoes

questions.text: Do you like buying shoes?
questions.answer: Yes, I like buying shoes because they are both useful and stylish. A new pair can make me feel confident and happy. Shoes also show a little of my personal style.

questions.text: Have you ever bought shoes online?
questions.answer: Yes, I have bought shoes online many times. It is convenient and saves me time. But sometimes the size is not right, so I prefer to try them in a shop.

questions.text: How much money do you usually spend on shoes?
questions.answer: I usually spend around 300 to 500 yuan on shoes. If the shoes are good quality, I don’t mind paying more. I think comfortable shoes are always worth the money.

questions.text: Which do you prefer, fashionable shoes or comfortable shoes?
questions.answer: I prefer comfortable shoes because I walk a lot every day. Fashionable shoes may look nice, but sometimes they hurt my feet. Comfort is always more important than style for me.

topics.title: Doing something well

questions.text: Do you have an experience when you did something well?
questions.answer: Yes, I remember once I gave a class presentation and it went really smoothly. I felt confident and my classmates seemed interested. It gave me a real sense of achievement.

questions.text: Do you have an experience when your teacher thought you did a good job?
questions.answer: Yes, my teacher once praised me for writing a clear and well-structured essay. She said I explained my ideas in a simple way. That made me feel really encouraged.

questions.text: Do you often tell your friends when they do something well?
questions.answer: Yes, I do. I think it’s important to cheer for your friends when they achieve something. A few kind words can make them feel proud and motivated.

topics.title: Crowded places

questions.text: Do you like crowded places?
questions.answer: No, I don’t like crowded places very much. They are usually noisy and stressful. When there are too many people, it’s hard to move around. I also feel tired after staying in a crowd. That’s why I prefer quiet places.

questions.text: Is the city where you live crowded?
questions.answer: Yes, the city where I live is quite crowded. There are many cars on the road every day. During rush hour, the streets are full of people and buses. Sometimes it takes a long time to travel even a short distance. So, yes, it is very crowded.

questions.text: Is there a crowded place near where you live?
questions.answer: Yes, near my home there is a big shopping mall. On weekends, it is always full of people. Families go there to shop, eat, and watch movies. The parking lot is also crowded with cars. It is the busiest place in my area.

questions.text: When was the last time you were in a crowded place?
questions.answer: The last time I was in a crowded place was last month. I went to a concert with my friends. The stadium was packed with people and very noisy. We had to wait in line for a long time to get in. It was fun but also tiring.

topics.title: Going out

questions.text: Do you bring good or snacks with you when going out?
questions.answer: I usually do bring some snacks with me when I go out—stuff like granola bars or fruit, ‘cause I often get hungry halfway through the day, and it saves me from having to grab expensive snacks on the go.Sometimes if I’m meeting friends for a walk or a trip to the park, I’ll also pack a small bag of chips or cookies to share—nothing too big, just enough to tide us over until we can get a proper meal later.

questions.text: Do you always take your mobile phone with you when going out?
questions.answer: I definitely always take my phone with me when I go out—It’s a total must-have, honestly. I use it for everything, like checking maps if I get lost, paying for coffee, or even texting friends to meet up somewhere, so I’d feel super stuck without it.The only time I might forget it is if I’m in a huge rush, but even then, I usually realize pretty quickly and end up doubling back home to grab it—losing or forgetting my phone feels like leaving part of myself behind!

topics.title: Working with old people

questions.text: Have you ever worked with old people?
questions.answer: Yes, I have. Back in school, I volunteered at a community center and helped some older people with daily activities. It was a nice experience because I learned a lot from their stories.

questions.text: Are you happy to work with people who are older than you?
questions.answer: Yes, I don’t mind at all. Older colleagues usually have more experience, and I can pick up useful skills from them. I think it makes the teamwork stronger.

questions.text: What are the advantages of working with old people?
questions.answer: One advantage is that they usually have more patience and knowledge. They can guide younger people and help solve problems more calmly. Working with them often feels reassuring.

topics.title: Growing vegetables / fruits

questions.text: Are you interested in growing vegetables and fruits?
questions.answer: Yes, I’m quite interested in it. I think it’s a healthy and relaxing activity. Growing vegetables gives me fresh food and also teaches me patience. It’s a good way to spend time outdoors.

questions.text: Is growing vegetables popular in your country?
questions.answer: Yes, it is popular, especially in the countryside. Many families have small gardens where they grow vegetables or fruits. In cities, some people also try balcony gardening. It’s becoming more common nowadays.

questions.text: Do you think it's easy to grow vegetables?
questions.answer: I think it’s not very easy, because it needs time and care. You have to water the plants regularly and protect them from insects. But if you learn the basic skills, it can become easier and enjoyable.

questions.text: Should schools teach students how to grow vegetables?
questions.answer: Yes, I think schools should teach this. It helps students understand where food comes from. It can also teach responsibility and teamwork when they grow plants together. It’s a useful life skill for the future.

topics.title: Chattting

questions.text: Do you like chatting with friends?
questions.answer: Yes, I really enjoy chatting with friends. It makes me feel relaxed and happy. We often share our daily stories and laugh together. Chatting also helps us understand each other better. For me, it’s an important part of friendship.

questions.text: What do you usually chat about with friends?
questions.answer: We usually chat about school, work, and hobbies. Sometimes we talk about movies or music we like. We also share our problems and give advice to each other. It’s nice to have someone to listen. Chatting makes our friendship stronger.

questions.text: Do you prefer to chat with a group of people or with only one friend?
questions.answer: I prefer to chat with only one friend. In a group, it is sometimes too noisy and I can’t say much. With one friend, I feel more comfortable and honest. It is easier to listen and understand. So I like small talks better.

questions.text: Do you argue with friends?
questions.answer: Sometimes I argue with friends, but not often. Most of the time we understand each other well. If we have different opinions, we try to talk calmly. After a short time, we usually make peace. I think real friends don’t stay angry for long.

topics.title: Borrowing and lending

questions.text: Have you borrowed books from others?
questions.answer: I have, but only once—last year when I forgot my wallet while out shopping, so I borrowed a small amount from my roommate to pay for groceries. I made sure to pay her back the next day because I hate owing people money, and I didn’t want her to think I was unreliable.

questions.text: Have you ever borrowed money from others?
questions.answer: I have, but only once—last year when I forgot my wallet while out shopping, so I borrowed a small amount from my roommate to pay for groceries. I made sure to pay her back the next day because I hate owing people money, and I didn’t want her to think I was unreliable.

questions.text: Do you like to lend things to others?
questions.answer: I don’t mind lending things to others, especially close friends or family who I know will take care of them—like a book or a kitchen tool, since it feels good to help someone out when they need it. But I’m a bit cautious about lending valuable or irreplaceable items, just because I’d be gutted if something got lost or broken.

questions.text: How do you feel when people don't return things they borrowed from you?
questions.answer: I usually feel a bit annoyed and let down when people don’t return borrowed things—especially if it’s something I use often, like my favorite notebook or a charger, because it messes up my daily routine. I try not to make a big deal out of it at first, but it does make me think twice about lending them things again later.

topics.title: Advertisement

questions.text: Do you see a lot of advertising on trains or other transport?
questions.answer: Yes, I often see many ads when I take the train or bus. They are usually about food, clothes, or mobile phones. Sometimes the ads are very colorful, so they catch my attention. But after a while, they feel a bit boring. Still, they are everywhere in public transport.

questions.text: Do you like commercials?
questions.answer: Honestly, I don’t really like commercials. Many of them are too long and repeat again and again. Sometimes they interrupt my favorite TV shows, which is annoying. But if the commercial is funny, I don’t mind watching it. I prefer short and creative ones.

questions.text: What kind of advertising do you like?
questions.answer: I like advertising that tells a story. For example, some ads show family love or friendship. They are warm and make me remember the brand. I also like ads with good music, because the song stays in my head. These ads are more meaningful.

questions.text: Is there an adverttisement that made an impression on you when you were a kid?
questions.answer: Yes, when I was a kid, I saw a milk advertisement on TV. It showed happy children drinking milk and playing outside. The music was very cheerful, and I remembered the slogan clearly. At that time, it made me want to drink milk every day. Even now I still remember it.

topics.title: Museum

questions.text: Do you think museums are important?
questions.answer: I definitely think museums are super important—they’re like treasure troves of history and culture, letting people get up close to artifacts and stories that you can’t just learn from a textbook. They also help keep traditions alive, especially for younger generations who might not otherwise get a chance to connect with their heritage or the wider world’s past.

questions.text: Do you often visit museums?
questions.answer: I don’t visit museums super often—maybe once every few months—usually when there’s a new exhibition that catches my eye, like a photography show or a history exhibit about a period I’m curious about. I tend to go with friends or family too, since chatting about what we see makes the visit more fun than going alone.

questions.text: When was the last time you visited a museum?
questions.answer: The last time I visited a museum was about two months ago—my cousin was in town, so we went to the local art museum together to check out its new exhibition on modern paintings. I spent around two hours there, and I even picked up a small souvenir from the gift shop to remember the day, since some of the artworks were really impressive.

topics.title: Having a break

questions.text: What do you usually do during a break?
questions.answer: During a break, I usually drink water or have a snack. Sometimes I check my phone for messages. If I have more time, I take a short walk. These small activities help me relax. After that, I can work better.

questions.text: What do you like to do during a break?
questions.answer: I like to listen to music during a break. It helps me forget stress for a while. Sometimes I chat with classmates or colleagues. A short talk can make me feel happy. Breaks give me energy to continue my work.

questions.text: Hos often do you take a break?
questions.answer: I usually take a short break every one or two hours. If I study or work for too long, I lose focus. A break helps me to stay fresh and clear-minded. It’s important not to work nonstop. Regular breaks improve my efficiency.

questions.text: Do you take a nap when you have a rest?
questions.answer: Yes, I often take a short nap when I have a rest. Even 15 or 20 minutes makes me feel much better. After a nap, I have more energy to continue working. But I try not to sleep too long. Otherwise, I feel lazy and slow.

topics.title: Sharing

questions.text: Did your parents teach you to share when you were a child?
questions.answer: Yes, my parents often taught me to share toys and snacks with my cousins and friends. They told me that sharing makes people happier and brings us closer. I think this habit helped me learn kindness and cooperation from an early age.

questions.text: What kinds of things do you like to share with others?
questions.answer: I like to share food, such as fruit or homemade dishes, with my friends. Sometimes I also share books or study materials with classmates. I think sharing knowledge and experiences is just as valuable as sharing things.

questions.text: Do you have anyting to share with others recently?
questions.answer: Yes, recently I bought some snacks during a trip, and I shared them with my colleagues. I also found a useful English learning app, and I recommended it to my classmates. Sharing makes me feel more connected to others.

questions.text: Who is the first person you would like to share good news with?
questions.answer: The first person I usually share good news with is my best friend. She always listens carefully and celebrates with me. Sometimes I also tell my parents, because I know they will be proud of me.

questions.answer: I’m studying a range of subjects like math, English, and science. This year, I’m really focusing on improving my grades in history and chemistry because they’re a bit harder for me.

part3.text: Why are some people more willing to protect wild animals than others?
part3.answer: Some people are more willing to protect wild animals because they feel a stronger sense of responsibility toward nature. They might also be more aware of environmental issues through education or personal experiences. Others may focus more on human needs and pay less attention to animals, so awareness really makes a difference.

part3.text: Do you think it's important to take children to the zoo to see animal?
part3.answer: Yes, I think it’s important, but in a balanced way. Zoos can help children learn about animals and develop empathy for them. At the same time, children should also be taught about protecting wildlife in their natural habitats, so they grow up with both knowledge and respect for nature.

topics.answer: One wild animal I really want to know more about is the snow leopard. I first saw it in a documentary a few years ago, and I was amazed by how beautiful and mysterious it looked. The snow leopard usually lives high up in the mountains, so it’s very rare to see one in real life. What interests me most is how it survives in such cold and harsh conditions, moving so quietly and blending into the rocks. I’d like to learn more about its habits, diet, and how people are trying to protect it. For me, the snow leopard represents strength and mystery, and I think learning about it would be really inspiring.
